newsitem.title: TURKEY: Gunmen shoot at Turkish TV station, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen shoot at Turkish TV station, no casualties.

text.p: Gunmen fired on the headquarters of a Turkish television channel in a drive-by shooting early on Wednesday, the latest in a series of attacks on media targets, Anatolian news agency said.
A shot fired from a passing car caused glass to shatter at the privately owned Interstar television station but there were no casualties, the agency said.
The attack took place three days after a bomb was thrown at a building housing the Hurriyet newspaper, which also caused no casualties.

A report by the Turkish journalists' union said this week that assaults on the media had reached dangerous levels. Five media organisations and two reporters were subject to armed attacks in May, the report said.

The report linked the attacks on the secularist media with current political turmoil, fuelled by a fierce row between the country's military and the outgoing Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan.
Erbakan's government publicly accused the mainstream media of stirring up tension between ruling the Islamists and the country's secularist elite.
Erbakan resigned last week as a result of the row with the military.
